sections.title: What the IP Header Is
sections.body: Every packet gets an IP header stuck on the front — like an envelope with a "from" and "to" address plus a few delivery notes. Routers read ONLY this header to move packets across the world. IPv4 header = 20 bytes (up to 60 with options).

head: Field
What it says
rows: How big the envelope itself is
Hops allowed; each router subtracts 1 — stops endless loops

sections.title: TTL — The Lifesaver
sections.body: Imagine two routers pointing at each other by mistake: a packet would bounce forever. TTL prevents this. It starts at 64 (or 128); every router subtracts 1. At 0 the packet is thrown away.
sections.code:
ping reply shows ttl=57
-> started at 64, passed through 7 routers

sections.title: Protocol Field = Which L4 Opens It
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: know 6=TCP, 17=UDP, 1=ICMP — and that TTL decreases by 1 at every router.
